Heavy rainfall and thunderstorms are expected across southern India, with Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, and Karaikal under an orange alert for intense downpours.
A low-pressure system in the Arabian Sea may intensify into a depression, prompting residents in vulnerable areas to stay alert and follow advisories.
Tamil Nadu faces an orange alert for heavy rain, with precipitation potentially reaching 204.4 mm.
Thunderstorms and gusty winds may cause waterlogging and disrupt traffic.
Andhra Pradesh, Kerala, and Karnataka are also bracing for unsettled weather with localized disruptions expected.
Heavy rainfall, thunderstorms and gusty winds are forecast across several southern Indian states, with Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal facing particularly intense downpours. Andhra Pradesh, Kerala and parts of Karnataka are also likely to experience unsettled weather.
Meanwhile, a low-pressure system over the southwest Arabian Sea could intensify into a depression within the next 24 hours before moving towards the Somali coast.
According to the latest weather update issued by the India Meteorological Department (IMD) on the morning of October 19, 2026, several regions are likely to experience rainfall accompanied by lightning and strong winds. Residents in vulnerable areas have been advised to remain alert and follow local weather advisories.
Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal are under an orange alert for heavy to very heavy rainfall in isolated areas, with precipitation potentially reaching 115.6–204.4 millimetres.
Thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds of 40–50 kilometres per hour are also forecast. Heavy downpours could cause waterlogging in low-lying areas, disrupt road traffic and create hazardous conditions for commuters.
The combination of heavy rainfall and strong winds could pose particular challenges in areas with inadequate drainage. Residents are advised to avoid unnecessary travel during severe weather, seek shelter during thunderstorms and monitor official forecasts.
Andhra Pradesh is also expected to receive heavy rainfall in isolated areas, prompting a yellow alert. Rainfall could range between 64.5 mm and 115.5 mm, with thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds reaching 40–50 km/h.
Kerala, Mahe and South Interior Karnataka are also likely to experience heavy rainfall. Thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and winds of 30–40km/h could cause localised disruption.
Residents in areas vulnerable to waterlogging and sudden changes in weather are advised to take precautions. People should seek shelter indoors during thunderstorms and avoid standing beneath trees or near electricity poles.
Unsettled weather is also forecast beyond southern India. The Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Lakshadweep, Telangana and parts of Interior Karnataka may experience thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds of 30-40 km/h.
Chhattisgarh, Coastal Karnataka, East Madhya Pradesh, Konkan and Goa, along with parts of Maharashtra, could also experience thunderstorms and lightning. West Madhya Pradesh may see thunderstorms accompanied by strong winds.
The intensity and timing of rainfall are likely to vary between districts, making local weather forecasts particularly important.
Meanwhile, a well-marked low-pressure area over the southwest Arabian Sea could intensify into a depression within the next 24 hours.
The system remained over approximately the same region at 5.30 am on October 19, after moving gradually eastwards.
The associated cyclonic circulation extended up to approximately 9.6 km above sea level. The system is initially expected to move east-northeastwards before gradually turning northwestwards towards the Somali coast over the following two to three days.
Its development and movement will continue to be monitored, with its potential effects depending on how the system evolves.
While parts of southern India prepare for heavy rainfall, high temperatures and substantial rainfall have been recorded elsewhere.
Rajkot in Gujarat recorded the country's highest maximum temperature of 39.9 degrees Celsius on 18 October. Mandi in Himachal Pradesh recorded a minimum temperature of 14.3 °C among the reported plains observations.
Madhya Pradesh also received substantial rainfall, with Guna recording 120 mm in the 24 hours ending at 5.30 am on October 19.
Digha in West Bengal received 20 mm, while Visakhapatnam, Ratnagiri, Gadag and Puri each recorded 10 mm.
Despite the unsettled conditions elsewhere, no major changes in weather are forecast across large parts of northwestern, central, eastern and northeastern India during the week.
A western disturbance and associated upper-level circulation near Himachal Pradesh and adjoining Punjab are not expected to have a significant impact on weather conditions across northern India.

Weather tomorrow October 20: IMD warns of rain, thunderstorms in Kerala, Karnataka, yellow alert in 17 Tamil Nadu districts – Check forecast for Delhi, Rajasthan, UP, Himachal

Check the latest weather forecast for Delhi, Noida, Gurugram, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Himachal Pradesh, Kerala and Karnataka.
Weather Forecast: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy monsoon rainfall and thunderstorms across several Indian states on Tuesday October 20. Heavy to very heavy rainfall has been predicted at isolated places in Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal, while downpours are likely over Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Coastal Andhra Pradesh and Kerala. Monsoon activities such as thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds are also expected in several parts. Meanwhile, weather researchers have spotted a low-pressure area which has formed over the southwest Arabian Sea, and it is expected to move towards the Somali coast by Saturday.
Delhi Weather
According to the weather department, most parts of Delhi and the adjoining National Capital Region (NCR), including Noida, Ghaziabad, Faridabad and Gurugram, will remain dry, with no rainfall predicted. No significant weather over the region during the week.
As per IMD, thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds are possible at isolated places over Konkan and Goa tomorrow. Central Maharashtra, including Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, Nashik, Ahmednagar (Ahilyanagar), Jalgaon, Dhule, Nandurbar, Beed, Jalna, Parbhani and Hingoli, are likely to experience thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds on October 20.
The IMD has reported a Western Disturbance over Himachal Pradesh and adjoining Punjab forming a cyclonic circulation. An associated trough in the middle tropospheric levels has also been spotted. Weather scientists also spotted a separate circulation over south Rajasthan and a trough over southwest Rajasthan.
Despite these atmospheric systems, no significant weather change is predicted over these states. Weather conditions will remain dry till Saturday.

Tamil Nadu, Puducherry Weather
Several parts of Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal may witness heavy to very heavy rainfall at isolated places on Tuesday. Isolated showers are expected across the region until October 25, with heavy rainfall during October 22-25. Thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds are possible at isolated places during October 19-25.
Kerala, Lakshadweep Weather
According to the weather department, most parts of Kerala and Mahe are expected to receive fairly widespread rainfall till October 25, with heavy rainfall at isolated places. Thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds are likely on October 20.
Similar weather conditions may persist in Lakshadweep, with widespread rainfall from October 19 to 25. Isolated heavy rainfall is also possible till October 25.
Karnataka Weather
Several parts of coastal Karnataka, including Mangaluru, Udupi, Karwar, Kundapura, Bhatkal, Honnavar, Kumta, Ankola and Mulki, are likely to receive isolated rainfall during October 19-22. Fairly widespread rainfall is forecast till October 24. Thunderstorms and lightning are likely at isolated places till October 23.
Tamil Nadu Weather
IMD has warned of heavy rainfall in several parts of Tamil Nadu on Tuesday, with isolated very heavy showers Puducherry and Karaikal till October 21. A yellow alert has been issued for 17 districts, including Chennai, Tiruvallur, Chengalpattu, Kancheepuram, Cuddalore and Tiruchi till Friday. Thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds are likely in parts of the state. Downpours are also expected at isolated places till October 24.
